We need to find a Costas array of order 9. A Costas array is a permutation of {0,...,n-1} such that the vectors (dr, dc) between pairs of points (c, x[c]) with dc > 0 are all distinct. That is, for any two pairs of columns c1 < c2 and c3 < c4, if c2 - c1 = c4 - c3 then we must have x[c2] - x[c1] != x[c4] - x[c3]. Equivalently, all the differences x[j] - x[i] for j > i must be unique for each difference j - i. Actually, the condition is: for each distance d = 1,...,n-1, the set of differences {x[i+d] - x[i] : i = 0,...,n-1-d} must consist of distinct values. Because if two pairs have same dc = d, then dr must be distinct. So for each d, the n-d differences must be all distinct.

perm = (0, 1, 5, 3, 8, 7, 4, 6, 2)

# Verify Costas property
n = len(perm)
vectors = []
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(i+1, n):
        dr = perm[j] - perm[i]
        dc = j - i
        vectors.append((dr, dc))

print(f"Number of vectors: {len(vectors)}")
print(f"Unique vectors: {len(set(vectors))}")
print(f"All vectors: {sorted(vectors)}")

# Check one per row and column
print(f"Is permutation: {sorted(perm) == list(range(n))}")
